title: Hockey stick $f$-divergences
authors: Fumio Hiai, Milán Mosonyi, Marco Tomamichel
abstract: In this paper we give a systematic and unified treatment and extensions of various results on a new notion of quantum $f$-divergences defined from quantum hockey stick divergences, the theory of which has been developed recently in \cite{BHT_fdiv,HircheTomamichel_integral,LiuHircheCheng2025}. In particular, we consider non-normalized states and hockey stick $f$-divergences defined from more general notions of quantum hockey stick divergences, as well as a somewhat more general form of the integral representation defined in terms of an additional real parameter. We also consider the extension of the theory to general von Neumann algebras, and extend various results from \cite{HircheTomamichel_integral,LiuHircheCheng2025} to this setting. Our main results here are the representation of the hockey stick $f$-divergences in terms of Neyman-Pearson error probabilities, which was given in the finite-dimensional case in \cite{LiuHircheCheng2025}, an extension of Jen\v cová's result \cite{Jencova2023} on the detection of reversibility of a quantum channel on a pair of states in terms of the hockey stick divergences, and an extension of a result in \cite{HircheTomamichel_integral} showing that the regularized hockey stick Rényi $α$-divergences coincide with the Petz-type Rényi divergences for $α\in(0,1)$ and with the sandwiched Rényi divergences for $α>1$. Moreover, we give some partial results on the characterization of when different notions of quantum $f$-divergences give the same value on a pair of quantum states.
summary: This paper develops a comprehensive theory for novel quantum $f$-divergences based on 'quantum hockey stick divergences.' It unifies various results by connecting these measures to classical hypothesis testing error probabilities and establishing relationships between different forms of Rényi divergences. The work extends these powerful mathematical tools from finite dimensions to the abstract setting of general von Neumann algebras.
main_problem: The paper aims to provide a systematic and unified treatment of quantum $f$-divergences, particularly those derived from 'quantum hockey stick divergences.'
main_result: Key results include representing these divergences using Neyman-Pearson error probabilities, extending detection criteria for quantum channel reversibility, and establishing connections between regularized Rényi $\alpha$-divergences and Petz/sandwiched Rényi divergences.
method: The work employs advanced mathematical tools from measure theory, functional analysis (convexity/concavity properties), and operator algebras to generalize classical $f$-divergence concepts to quantum states.
model_or_system: The theory applies to quantum states described by density operators ($\varrho, \sigma$) on a Hilbert space, with extensions formulated for general von Neumann algebras.
key_observables: Quantum $f$-divergences (measured and maximal), hockey stick $f$-divergences, and their representations in terms of Neyman-Pearson error probabilities.
important_parameters: The analysis involves a real parameter $\alpha$ for Rényi divergences, and the theory is developed across finite dimensions up to general von Neumann algebras.
main_assumptions: The mathematical derivations rely on properties like positive homogeneity, existence of derivatives (left/right), and assumptions about the underlying measure spaces ($\nu \ll \mu$).
paper_structure: The paper progresses logically from reviewing classical $f$-divergences to tackling finite-dimensional quantum divergences using hockey stick methods, extending this theory to general von Neumann algebras, and finally analyzing regularized Rényi $\alpha$-divergences.
why_interesting: While highly mathematical, the generalization of divergence measures (like relative entropy) is fundamental for quantifying distinguishability between quantum states, which is crucial in understanding open quantum systems dynamics and process characterization.
